### Signals Before Waking

Preparation may not be a last-second switch. In one study, seven successful participants showed right prefrontal changes about 30 minutes before waking; in a small nap study, heart rate began rising about three minutes beforehand. Different systems may therefore join the transition on different timelines, rather than one signal predicting an exact alarm minute.

### Why It Can Feel Easy

Sleep itself changes across the night. Deep slow-wave sleep is more common earlier, while lighter NREM and REM sleep become more common later. Because waking from deep N3 sleep produces stronger sleep inertia than waking from N2, a near-alarm awakening may feel clearer simply because the brain is in a gentler stage—not because it has read the clock.

## In one line

The morning mystery may be less like a hidden alarm and more like several modest systems meeting at the right moment. That can feel uncanny without requiring perfect prediction.
